mainTopic: Moving objects on שבת: תורת כלי, the window shutter, covers of vessels and of the ground, and clearing baskets for guests and learning.
overview: The amud opens by settling a contradiction in רבי יוחנן's rulings. He ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, yet he requires that an item have real תורת כלי. The answer is that he agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on one point and disagrees on another. Next, רבי יצחק נפחא rules like רבי אליעזר about the window shutter. רב עמרם challenges him from a משנה, and the גמרא concludes that a recorded action (מעשה רב) carries the most weight. A משנה about moving covers on שבת follows, and the גמרא explains that the תנאים argue only about a special case: vessels attached to the ground, or, in another version, an oven cover. The chapter כל הכלים then ends. A new chapter opens with a משנה about clearing baskets for guests and for learning, and about which foods and bundles may be moved on שבת. The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions 'four' baskets when five are allowed, and רב חסדא answers. שמואל begins a different answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן requires real vessel status for lids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the סתם משנה about lids with handles. It then adds רבי יוחנן's own condition that the lid must have תורת כלי, which seems to clash with his ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Lids of vessels] that have a handle may be moved on שבת. And רב יהודה בר שילא said in the name of רב אסי, in the name of רבי יוחנן: that is only when the lid has the status of a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a challenge it began on the previous amud. רבי יוחנן said the lid rule applies only if the lid counts as a real כלי, so he seems to require more than רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יוחנן ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says simply preparing a reed for use is enough to allow moving it. Here רבי יוחנן adds that an object must have actual תורת כלי. That is a stricter standard than mere preparation, so his two statements appear to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle; a place to grip the item
May be moved (not מוקצה)
The legal status of a vessel or utensil
Lids or covers of vessels (the subject of this משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a quote. The first words finish the משנה 'כיסוי הכלים בזמן שיש להם בית אחיזה', which began earlier.

phrases.english: that Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
And that is when the status of a vessel applies to them.
phrases.notes: Adds a stricter condition: real vessel status

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun earlier against רבי יוחנן ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן requires actual תורת כלי, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that preparation alone is enough. So רבי יוחנן cannot fully agree with him.

steps.title: Blocking the answer that the reed also has vessel status
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reed also has תורת כלי. The גמרא rejects this using a ברייתא in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows palm branches to be used for sitting even without tying them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too the reed has vessel status, does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל even require vessel status? But a ברייתא teaches: palm branches that someone cut for firewood, and then he changed his mind and decided to sit on them, must be tied together. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: they do not need to be tied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines an answer to the contradiction and then shuts it down. A ברייתא shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל never requires real vessel status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed answer was that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's case also involves a real כלי, so there is no contradiction. The ברייתא disproves this. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, just deciding to use the branches for sitting is enough, with no physical action such as tying. So he truly does not require תורת כלי, and the contradiction with רבי יוחנן stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer that the גמרא will reject)
Hard branches of a palm tree
He reconsidered or changed his plan
To tie together (a physical act that makes them usable as a seat)

steps.confusionAlert: 'וכי תימא' is not the גמרא's real answer. It raises a possible reply only so it can knock it down.

phrases.english: And if you say: here too

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי בָּעֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: does Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel require
that the status of a vessel apply to it?
But was it not taught: hard branches of a palm tree
that one cut for firewood,
and then he reconsidered them for sitting,
he must tie them (before Shabbat).
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He need not tie them.
phrases.notes: Thought alone is enough for him

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי דְּאִיכָּא תּוֹרַת כְּלִי עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible defense of רבי יוחנן, which strengthens the contradiction from Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested defense that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reed also has תורת כלי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits moving an item based on intention alone, with no physical act. So he does not require real vessel status.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן agrees on one point and disagrees on another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on one issue and argues with him on another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן agrees with him on one point and disagrees with him on one point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רבי יוחנן's statement 'the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל' was only partial agreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that the reed does not need to be tied and hanging. He disagrees with him by requiring that the item have real תורת כלי, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל accepts intention alone. So both of רבי יוחנן's statements stand without contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like him; agrees with him
In one matter
He disagrees with him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that no tying is needed, but he requires real תורת כלי.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan holds like him in one matter
and disagrees with him in one matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial agreement: the ruling 'like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל' is limited to one aspect.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed that ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל meant accepting his whole view, including that intention alone is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן adopts only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's leniency about tying, and he keeps his own requirement of תורת כלי.

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא rules like רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: A new section opens. רבי יצחק נפחא publicly teaches that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר about the window shutter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא taught at the entrance of the house of the ריש גלותא: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to a new question: whose opinion in the משנה is the final הלכה. רבי יצחק נפחא rules like רבי אליעזר, and this sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר allows sealing a window with a shutter only if it was tied and hanging, meaning prepared beforehand. The חכמים permit it either way. Ruling like רבי אליעזר means taking the stricter view.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded or taught publicly
At the entrance
The Exilarch, head of the Babylonian Jewish community
The final law follows (someone)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nafcha taught publicly
at the entrance of the house of the Exilarch:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: Regarding the window shutter: it must be tied and hanging

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַשׁ רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אַפִּתְחָא דְרֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the final ruling in the משנה's dispute about the window shutter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר: a window shutter may be used only if it was tied and hanging.

steps.title: רב עמרם objects from a משנה that permits sealing
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם challenges רבי יצחק נפחא with a משנה stating that the sages' words and actions taught that one may seal, measure, and tie on Shabbat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם raised an objection: 'And from their statements we learned that one may seal, measure, and tie on שבת!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם attacks the ruling like רבי אליעזר. He cites a משנה that permits sealing on Shabbat without mentioning any condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says one may seal, with no condition that the item was tied or prepared. That fits the חכמים, not רבי אליעזר. So it seems the הלכה should not follow רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: We seal or plug (an opening)
We measure
We tie (a knot)

phrases.english: Rav Amram raised an objection:
And from their statements we learned
that one may seal, and measure, and tie on Shabbat!
phrases.notes: Sealing is allowed here with no need to prepare anything beforehand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges the ruling stated in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק נפחא's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה permits sealing on Shabbat with no condition of tying or preparation. That matches the חכמים and goes against רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: אביי: The bolt משנה is also unattributed
steps.stepSummary: אביי weakens רב עמרם's proof. If his proof works because his source is a סתם משנה, the משנה about the dragged bolt (נגר הנגרר) is also a סתם משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What are you thinking? That your proof works because the משנה is taught without a name? The משנה about the dragged bolt is also taught without a name!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב עמרם's challenge. He points out that the other side also has an unattributed משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב עמרם seemed to rely on the rule that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה. אביי answers that the משנה of נגר הנגרר, which matches רבי אליעזר's view, is also a סתם משנה. So the two sources seem to cancel each other out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your reasoning / what are you thinking?
Unattributed; a ruling taught with no name attached (a סתם משנה)
A dragged bolt, meaning a door bolt that is tied on and hangs or drags

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: Said to רב עמרם.

phrases.english: What is your thinking?
Because it is taught without attribution?
phrases.notes: The rule is that the הלכה usually follows a סתם משנה.

phrases.english: The dragged bolt is also an unattributed משנה!
phrases.notes: That משנה allows a bolt only when it is attached, which matches רבי אליעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עמרם's challenge (step 5) by showing that his proof can be matched by an equal source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the proof wins because it is a סתם משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The opposing side also has a סתם משנה, so being unattributed does not decide the question.

steps.title: Even so, a real practice is stronger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב עמרם's source still wins. It contains an actual story of what the חכמים did, and a recorded action carries more weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even so, an action is greater.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the debate. It accepts that both sources are סתם משניות, but רב עמרם's source wins because it reports what the חכמים actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב עמרם's משנה does more than state a rule. It records the חכמים' own practice ("their words and their actions"). A real-life precedent is stronger than a plain statement, so it outweighs the נגר הנגרר משנה, and רבי יצחק נפחא's ruling is challenged after all.

keyTerms.meaning: And even so
An action is greater: a real-life precedent carries special weight

steps.whatToRemember: When two sources seem equal, a source that records what the חכמים actually did (מעשה רב) beats a source that only states a rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: מעשה רב is a general principle used across ש״ס for deciding הלכה.

phrases.english: And even so,
an action is greater.
phrases.notes: A recorded practice outweighs a plain statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's point by finding something that makes רב עמרם's source stronger after all.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב עמרם's source wins because it contains a מעשה (a recorded practice). This weakens רבי יצחק נפחא's ruling like רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: משנה: Moving covers on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that covers with a handle may be moved on שבת. רבי יוסי limits the handle requirement to covers of the ground. Covers of vessels may be moved either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All covers of vessels that have a handle may be moved on שבת. רבי יוסי said: When was this said? For covers of the ground. But covers of vessels may be moved on שבת either way.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: which covers may be moved on שבת. There are two opinions, the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא seems to require a handle for every cover. רבי יוסי says the handle matters only for a cover of the ground, such as the cover of a pit. A cover of a vessel may be moved whether or not it has a handle.

keyTerms.meaning: Covers of vessels (lids)
A handle, a place to grip it
May be moved (not מוקצה)
Covers of the ground, such as the cover of a pit
Either way: with or without a handle

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
All covers of vessels
that have a handle
may be moved on Shabbat.
Rabbi Yosei said:
In what case was this said?
For covers of the ground,
phrases.notes: For example, the cover of a pit.

phrases.english: but for covers of vessels,
either way,
phrases.notes: With or without a handle.

phrases.english: they may be moved on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל כִּיסּוּיֵי הַכֵּלִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם בֵּית אֲחִיזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Covers with handles may be moved on שבת. According to רבי יוסי, the handle is needed only for covers of the ground, not for covers of vessels.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The cover must count as a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds a condition: the cover may be moved only if it has the status of a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה בר שילא said in the name of רבי אסי, in the name of רבי יוחנן: And this applies only when the cover has the status of a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a limit on the משנה. A cover may be moved only if it has תורת כלי (the status of a vessel).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A handle alone is not enough. The cover must itself be a real, usable object (a כלי). If it is just a random piece of material, it stays מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The status of a vessel: a real, usable object
And this applies only when (introduces a condition)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda bar Sheila said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
And this applies when they have the status of a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְהוּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ תּוֹרַת כְּלִי עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the משנה's permission to move covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Covers may be moved only if they have the status of a כלי.

steps.title: What everyone agrees on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that both תנאים agree on the basic cases. A ground cover needs a handle, and a vessel cover does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees: covers of the ground, if they have a handle, yes; if not, no. Covers of vessels may be moved even if they have no handle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. Before showing where the תנאים argue, it first lists the cases where they agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This changes how we read the משנה. The תנא קמא also agrees that a normal vessel cover needs no handle. So the argument must be about some other, special case.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees (both opinions)
Yes
Even though

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the תנא קמא as requiring a handle on every vessel cover. The גמרא says he agrees that a regular vessel cover needs no handle.

phrases.english: Everyone agrees: covers of the ground,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לָהֶן בֵּית אֲחִיזָה — אִין,
phrases.english: if they have a handle, yes (they may be moved);
if not, no.
Covers of vessels

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין לָהֶם בֵּית אֲחִיזָה.
phrases.english: may be moved even though they have no handle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinterprets the משנה by narrowing the range of the disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ground covers need a handle and vessel covers do not. Both תנאים agree on this.

steps.title: The real argument: vessels attached to the ground
steps.stepSummary: The תנאים argue only about vessels that were attached to the ground. The תנא קמא makes a גזירה, and רבי יוסי does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is about vessels that one attached to the ground. One master holds we make a decree, and the other holds we do not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the exact case the תנאים argue about: a vessel that has been fixed into the ground. It also gives the reason for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cover of an attached vessel looks like a ground cover. The תנא קמא forbids moving it without a handle, out of fear that people will come to move real ground covers without handles. רבי יוסי does not make that גזירה, since it is still a cover of a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they disagree
That one attached to the ground
We make a protective decree (גזירה)
One master holds

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees on the basic cases. The only argument is whether to make a גזירה for a vessel attached to the ground: the תנא קמא does, and רבי יוסי does not.

phrases.english: Where they disagree
is about vessels that one attached to the ground.
This master holds we make a decree,
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא, who fears confusion with ground covers.

phrases.english: and that master holds we do not make a decree.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing the points of agreement (step 10), the גמרא names the one disputed case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's argument is limited to vessels attached to the ground, and it depends on whether we make a גזירה because of ground covers.

steps.title: A second version: the argument is only about an oven cover
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, the תנאים argue only about the cover of an oven. One side treats it like a ground cover, and the other treats it like a vessel cover.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: When they argue, it is about the cover of an oven. One master compares it to a ground cover, and the other master compares it to a vessel cover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different explanation of what the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי argue about. This version says the argument is about an oven cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, the argument was about vessels that had been attached to the ground, and it depended on a גזירה. Here there is no גזירה. The only question is how to classify an oven cover. An oven is built into the ground but is also a kind of vessel. If its cover counts as a כיסוי קרקע, it needs a handle. If it counts as a כיסוי כלים, it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version: a second way the explanation was handed down
The cover of an oven
Compares it to; treats it as similar to
A cover for something in the ground, such as a pit

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the dispute. Version 1: they argue about vessels that were attached to the ground, and it depends on a גזירה. Version 2: they argue about an oven cover, and it depends on whether it is like a ground cover or a vessel cover. In both versions, a ground cover needs a handle and a vessel cover does not.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new challenge to step 11. It is a different tradition of the same explanation, and it stands side by side with the first version.

phrases.english: and the other master compares it to a vessel cover.
phrases.notes: So it would not need a handle

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּכִיסּוּי תַּנּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of step 11's explanation of where the תנאים disagree
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the second version, the dispute is only about how to classify an oven cover: is it like a ground cover or like a vessel cover?

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כל הכלים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter כל הכלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'כל הכלים'.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter כל הכלים ends here. This is the traditional closing line said when finishing a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן means 'we will return.' It shows love for the learning and a hope to come back and learn this chapter again. No new הלכה is taught here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula said at the end of a chapter
The name of the chapter that just ended, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'All the Vessels'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that steps 1–12 belonged to

steps.title: Clearing many baskets for guests or for learning, but not the storeroom
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה allows clearing away even four or five baskets of straw or grain on שבת to make room for guests or for the בית המדרש. It does not allow clearing the אוצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may clear away even four or five baskets of straw and of grain because of guests, and so that learning in the בית המדרש is not stopped. But one may not clear the storeroom.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It allows a fairly big job on שבת, clearing away several baskets, when the space is needed for guests or for Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving many heavy baskets is a lot of work, and we might think it is not proper on שבת. The משנה allows it because the purpose is a מצוה: hosting guests (הכנסת אורחים) or making room for learning. The limit is the אוצר, a stored-up pile, and the גמרא explains this limit in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: One may clear away or move (to make space)
Baskets
Straw
Guests
Stopping or disrupting learning in the study hall
A storeroom or a stored-up pile of produce

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a מצוה need, such as guests or תורה learning, can justify extra effort on שבת. There is still a limit.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may clear away
phrases.notes: The opening word, which also gives the new chapter its name

phrases.english: even four or five baskets
of straw and of grain
because of the guests
phrases.notes: To make room for them to sit

phrases.english: and so that learning in the study hall is not stopped.
But not the storeroom.
phrases.notes: The גמרא explains this limit in step 23

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מְפַנִּין אֲפִילּוּ אַרְבַּע וְחָמֵשׁ קוּפּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clearing even many baskets is allowed for guests or for the בית המדרש, but the אוצר may not be cleared.

steps.title: Foods that may be moved because someone can use them
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists foods that may be moved on שבת: pure תרומה, דמאי, מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken, redeemed מעשר שני and הקדש, and dry lupine, which is goat food.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may move pure תרומה, דמאי, מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was already taken, מעשר שני and הקדש that were redeemed, and dry lupine, because it is food for goats.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a list of foods that may be moved on שבת. Each one is usable by somebody, so it is not מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item looks at first like it might be off-limits, but each is fit for someone. Pure תרומה is fit for a כהן. דמאי, tithed first tithe, and redeemed מעשר שני and הקדש are fit for people to eat. Dry lupine is too hard for people, but goats eat it, and that is enough. The משנה continues afterward with the opposite list of foods that may not be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure תרומה, which a כהן may eat
Produce bought from an עם הארץ, where we are unsure whether it was tithed
First tithe, given to a לוי
That were redeemed (their holiness was moved onto money)
Lupine, a hard bean
Food for goats

steps.confusionAlert: Something does not have to be edible for you to be movable. It is enough that some person, or even an animal, can use it.

phrases.english: One may move pure teruma, and demai,
and first tithe whose teruma has been taken,
and second tithe and consecrated items that were redeemed,
and dry lupine
because it is food for goats.
phrases.notes: This reason applies to the dry lupine: people cannot eat it, but goats can, so it is not מוקצה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a second ruling about which foods may be moved
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Foods that are fit for some person or animal may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: Foods that may not be moved on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists foods that may NOT be moved on שבת: טבל, מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken, unredeemed מעשר שני and הקדש, לוף, and mustard.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you may not move טבל, or מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken, or מעשר שני and הקדש that were not redeemed, or לוף, or mustard.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list from the last step. It now gives the opposite side: foods that are forbidden to move on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item here mirrors an item on the 'allowed' list. The allowed list had fixed or redeemed foods, and this list has the same foods before they were fixed or redeemed. These foods cannot be eaten on שבת, because you may not separate tithes or redeem on שבת, so they are מוקצה. לוף and mustard are not eaten raw by people, so they are not seen as ready food.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תְּרוּמָה and מַעַשְׂרוֹת have not yet been taken; forbidden to eat
Were redeemed (exchanged for money to remove their holiness)
A type of arum plant, not eaten raw by people
Mustard

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up לוף with the dry lupine (תורמוס) from the previous step. The lupine was permitted as goat food. לוף is a different plant.

phrases.english: But not tevel (untithed produce),

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת מַעֲשֵׂר [רִאשׁוֹן] שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְּרוּמָתוֹ,
phrases.english: and not first tithe whose teruma was not taken,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ,
phrases.english: and not second tithe and consecrated items that were not redeemed,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַלּוּף, וְלָא אֶת הַחַרְדָּל.
phrases.english: and not arum (luf), and not mustard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list from step 15 by giving the forbidden counterparts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Foods not yet fixed, not yet redeemed, or not fit for people (לוף, mustard) are מוקצה and may not be moved.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits לוף
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits moving לוף because ravens eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits לוף, because it is food for ravens.
steps.whatsHappening: A dissenting opinion is added to the last item. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees about לוף and allows it to be moved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is the same one that permitted the dry lupine: if it is food for some creature, it has a use and is not מוקצה. The תנא קמא does not count raven food as a real use.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits
Ravens

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַתִּיר בַּלּוּף,
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits arum,
because it is food for ravens.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַתִּיר בַּלּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with one item (לוף) on the forbidden list in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוף may be moved because it serves as food for ravens.

steps.title: Bundles of straw, wood, and twigs
steps.stepSummary: Bundles of straw, wood, or twigs may be moved on שבת only if they were prepared as animal food. Otherwise they may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bundles of straw, bundles of wood, and bundles of twigs: if he prepared them as animal food, they may be moved. If not, they may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule about bundles that are usually meant for fuel or building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items are normally not food, so by default they are מוקצה. If the owner set them aside ahead of time (before שבת) as animal feed, he gives them a permitted use, and they may be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: Bundles of
Twigs / small branches
He prepared them (designated them in advance)
We may move them

steps.whatToRemember: Designating an item for a permitted use before שבת can take it out of מוקצה.

phrases.aramaic: חֲבִילֵי קַשׁ וַחֲבִילֵי עֵצִים וַחֲבִילֵי זְרָדִים,
phrases.english: Bundles of straw, and bundles of wood, and bundles of twigs,
if he prepared them for animal food —
one may move them.
And if not — one may not move them.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲבִילֵי קַשׁ וַחֲבִילֵי עֵצִים וַחֲבִילֵי זְרָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the משנה, about non-food items that can become usable as animal feed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bundles prepared as animal food may be moved. Unprepared bundles are מוקצה.

steps.title: Why mention four if five is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking: if the משנה allows clearing five baskets, why does it also need to say four?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Now that one may clear five, is it necessary to say four?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins, going back to the משנה in step 14 about clearing 'four or five baskets.' It challenges the wording, because the word 'four' seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If five baskets are allowed, then four are obviously allowed too. So listing 'four' seems pointless. The גמרא assumes every word of a משנה teaches something, so it asks what 'four' adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that (if X is true already)
We clear away
Is it necessary to say?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Now that one may clear five,
is four necessary to say?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה in step 14 to question its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'four or five baskets' in the משנה of step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Allowing five already includes four, so mentioning four is redundant.

steps.title: רב חסדא: four out of five
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the משנה means four baskets out of five: you may clear some of the pile, but not all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Four out of five.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. 'Four or five' is not two separate numbers. It means 'four out of a pile of five.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, 'five' describes the size of the pile and 'four' is how many you may remove. So neither word is extra, and the limit is that you may not empty the pile completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Four out of five

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Four out of five,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Four and five are two separate permitted amounts, so four is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Five is the size of the pile, and four is the most you may remove from it.

steps.title: Second version: small storeroom and large storeroom
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רב חסדא's answer: you may clear four baskets from a small storeroom and five from a large storeroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Four from a small storeroom, and five from a large storeroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב חסדא's answer. Here each number applies to a different size of storeroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, both numbers are real limits, but for different cases. A small storeroom allows only four, and a large storeroom allows five, so 'four' is not redundant.

keyTerms.meaning: A small storeroom
A large storeroom

steps.confusionAlert: The parentheses mark 'איכא דאמרי ארבע מאוצר קטן' as a printed gloss. רש״י reads 'וחמש מאוצר גדול' as the end of רב חסדא's own statement: four out of a small pile of five, and five from a large storeroom. This breakdown follows the reading that splits the line into two versions.

phrases.english: (Some say:
four from a small storeroom)
and five from a large storeroom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative version of the answer in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the numbers into two different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Four is redundant once five is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Four applies to a small storeroom and five to a large one.

steps.title: What does 'but not the storeroom' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means when it says you may clear baskets, 'but not the storeroom.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does it mean, 'but not the storeroom'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still working inside רב חסדא's explanation of the משנה. It now asks about the last phrase: 'but not the storeroom.' This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed clearing baskets of produce from a storeroom. Then it said 'but not the storeroom,' which sounds like a contradiction. The גמרא wants to know what exactly is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A storeroom, a place where produce is stored for a long time
And what (does it mean)?

phrases.english: And what does 'but not the storeroom' mean?
phrases.notes: Quoting the end of the משנה's ruling

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב חסדא's reading of the משנה by now explaining its final phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of the משנה's words 'but not the storeroom.'

steps.title: Do not start on a storeroom for the first time
steps.stepSummary: 'But not the storeroom' means you may not begin clearing a storeroom for the first time on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that he should not begin with the storeroom for the first time (on שבת).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The משנה is not forbidding all storeroom produce. It only forbids starting on a storeroom that nobody had begun using before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the storeroom was already opened and used before שבת, you may take baskets from it. If it was never touched, its produce was not set aside for use, so you may not open it up on שבת. This resolves the apparent contradiction in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: That he should not begin
For the first time, at the start

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean storerooms are totally off-limits. It only means you may not be the first to start on an untouched storeroom on שבת.

phrases.english: that he should not begin with the storeroom for the first time,
phrases.notes: That is, a storeroom not yet opened before שבת

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The forbidden act is opening a fresh, untouched storeroom on שבת. Taking from one already opened before שבת is allowed.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the author of this משנה as רבי יהודה, because he holds the rule of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose opinion is this? It is רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names whose opinion the משנה follows. It is רבי יהודה, because he holds that things not set aside for use before שבת are מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce sitting in a storeroom nobody has started is not mentally set aside for use, so it counts as מוקצה. Only someone who holds of מוקצה would forbid starting a new storeroom. That fits רבי יהודה, not רבי שמעון, who is lenient about מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: And who is (the author)?
Set aside, not designated for use before שבת, and so forbidden to move
Who holds (this opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: In רב חסדא's approach, the משנה allows clearing some baskets from a storeroom already opened before שבת. It forbids starting a new one. This follows רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ban on starting a storeroom is a מוקצה issue. That is why it depends on whether one holds like רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And who is the author? It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who holds of muktze (set-aside items).
phrases.notes: Untouched storeroom produce was not designated for use, so it is מוקצה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind step 23's rule by naming the opinion it follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה.

steps.title: שמואל begins a different answer: 'four and five'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל offers a new answer to the question of why the משנה says both 'four' and 'five' baskets. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: 'Four and five'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings שמואל, who answers the original question from step 19 differently from רב חסדא. Only his opening words appear here. His full explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא gave each number its own legal meaning, either 'four out of five' or a small versus a large storeroom. שמואל is about to explain that 'four or five' is just a common figure of speech, not an exact number. So the word 'four' is not truly redundant, and there is no difficulty to solve.

keyTerms.meaning: And שמואל said (introducing a different opinion)
Four and five, the numbers being explained

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: Four and five,
phrases.notes: His explanation (a figure of speech) continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question of step 19 and offers an alternative to רב חסדא's answers in steps 20-21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording as a figure of speech rather than an exact number (explained on the next amud).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה gives 'four' and 'five' as two exact amounts, which seems redundant.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל will explain that 'four or five' is a loose, everyday expression, not a precise limit.
